title: regional-gentle-drain-and-transparent-restore-conductor
author: Avery Patel
release_notes: Implements a tenant-aware gentle drain plus transparent restore conductor to reduce noisy failovers during regional capacity shifts; improves SLO stability and KV-replay safety; backport to 2026.2 recommended for critical regions.
description: Motivation: During the Feb regional surge incident we observed aggressive tenant drains that caused cascading retries and KV cache inconsistencies when traffic returned. This PR introduces a coordinated 'Gentle Drain and Transparent Restore Conductor' that reduces noisy failovers by doing two things: (1) a tenant-aware gentle-drain algorithm that imposes a soft ramp-down with token-limited acceptance windows, and (2) a transparent-restore flow that preserves per-tenant KV snapshot markers and allows safe replay/rehydration on node rejoin. Design summary: - Gentle drain: tenant scoring is extended with a decay-aware backoff that reduces abrupt evictions; new parameters allow configurable ramp-duration, token-cap-per-window, and weight hysteresis so high-priority tenants do not suffer unnecessary SLO relaxation. - Transparent restore: on node demotion or planned drain we create compact KV snapshots with an idempotent replay marker; nodes rejoining will perform a checksum-validated state-sync and only accept replayed requests up to the last stable marker to avoid double-processing. - Circuit harmonizer: we add short-term circuit strobing protection so neighbouring regional circuits do not flip state in lockstep (prevents resonance). - Canary/rollout: the feature is gated behind a runtime flag and a per-region canary that primes with low-rate production traffic using token-limited warmup. Backwards compatibility: runtime flags keep original behavior intact. For Private deployments the restore flow falls back to current KV-drain path if state-sync is disabled. Testing: unit tests added for the scoring decay and token window; integration harness simulates a three-region failover with staggered drains and verifies no duplicate outputs for idempotent requests; a soak job ran for 48 hours in staging with mixed tenant weights. Rollout plan: 1) merge to main behind feature flag, 2) enable in a single low-traffic region for 24h canary, 3) expand to additional regions with telemetry checks, 4) enable auto-fallback to legacy drain if rollback signal observed. Checklist: - [x] design doc updated (RFC-DR-631) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] telemetry hooks and histograms added - [x] graceful rollback path implemented - [x] documented runtime config in ops wiki Observability/metrics added: tenant_drain_rate{region}, drain_token_utilization, restore_replay_success, restore_replay_conflicts, circuit_resync_count. Operational playbook: added instructions to the SRE runbook for forced-restore, manual marker prune, and emergency-disable flag. Related: follows up on ENG-1987 and SUP-4391 incident notes. Notes: this PR intentionally keeps the throttle knobs conservative (default ramp-duration = 60s, token-cap = 250 r/s) to avoid surprise on high-throughput tenants. The team will adjust after canary telemetry.

review_comments: Elena Kuznetsova: Nice approach. Two quick asks: (1) describe how markers behave across shard resizes, (2) please ensure restore_replay_conflicts is a counter not a gauge.

Avery Patel (author): Markers are stable per-tenant per-shard id; on resize we write a tombstone marker and the restore flow merges by last-writer-with-epoch. I'll change the metric to a counter and add comments explaining the shard-resize merge semantics.

Marcus Lee: Can we add a short-circuit for very small tenants so they don't pay the extra snapshot cost? Also add a safety net that disables transparent restore if the snapshot store latency exceeds threshold.
Avery Patel (author): Added small-tenant bypass with configurable threshold and a snapshot-store-latency health check that flips the fallback flag. See configs/ops_runtime.yaml for knobs.
Samira Thompson: CI flaked on integration initially (race in rehydration). After fix I re-ran and tests passed. Approving pending telemetry names standardized.
notes: Hotfix sensitivity: although this is feature-gated, ops prefers a backport to the 2026.2 maintenance branch for regions with frequent transient surges. Coordinated rollouts with the marketplace teams (APAC regions) are scheduled in the ops calendar.
post_merge_actions: Enable feature flag in staging for region us-west-2 on 2026-02-22; monitor tenant_drain_rate and restore_replay_conflicts; after 24h expand to eu-central-1; schedule 1-week follow-up to tune token-cap defaults.
impact_summary: Expected reduction in cascading retries and duplicate processing when nodes rejoin after drains. Slight increase in snapshot store writes for medium-large tenants (configurable). Overall SLO stability improvement in surge scenarios.
